content.text: Section 23 ("RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE") is heading-only with no substantive text, so there is no separate records/assurance audit right. Section 22 is the sole audit provision binding us, and it matches every element of the preferred position.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 is the only audit/verification right binding us as Customer, and it meets or exceeds every element of the preferred position: frequency capped at once in any twelve-month period (22.1); thirty days' prior written notice (22.1); normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption (22.1); off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1); Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and then only reasonable costs plus the undisputed shortfall (22.2); and an express bar on Vendor or its auditor accessing Customer systems directly, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information (22.2). Section 22.3 adds further customer-favourable protection by making audit findings Customer Confidential Information, restricting use to enforcement, requiring delivery of the final report, and making payment of a shortfall resolve the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error. I confirmed there is no separate or overlapping audit right elsewhere: a full-text search for audit/inspect/verify/monitor/records/examine/assurance surfaced no other clause imposing verification obligations on us, and Section 23 ("RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE"), which the planner flagged as a risk, contains only the heading paragraph with no operative text. Section 26.4 runs the other way (Vendor must follow our policies when accessing our facilities or systems) and so benefits us. No redline is warranted.
